subtopics.title: Why Assets Lose Value in the Books

questions.question: Matching requires depreciation because:
options: The asset earns income across many years, so its cost must be spread as an expense across those same years
Assets must be revalued upward annually
All costs belong to the year of purchase

questions.question: The three figures to keep apart are:
options: COST (anchored at purchase), ACCUMULATED depreciation (the growing write-off), CARRYING value (cost minus accumulated)
Purchase price, selling price and mark-up

questions.question: The annual double entry for depreciation is:
options: Debit Depreciation (expense), credit Accumulated Depreciation — never the asset account itself

questions.question: The Vehicles account never moves after purchase because:
options: Depreciation is not a real expense
The bookkeeper may not touch asset accounts
Historical cost anchors the recorded cost; the wearing gathers in the counter-account instead

questions.question: The bakkie: R120 000 at 20% p.a. on cost. Every year's depreciation is:
options: R24 000 — the same slice, because the base (cost) never changes
R24 000 in year one, then less each year

questions.question: At the end of year two (straight-line), the three figures are:
options: Cost R96 000; accumulated R24 000; carrying R72 000
Cost R120 000; accumulated R48 000; carrying value R72 000
Cost R120 000; accumulated R24 000; carrying R96 000
Cost R72 000; accumulated R48 000; carrying R24 000

questions.question: At 20% on cost, the whole cost is consumed in:
options: Five years — though the books often leave R1 standing while the asset still works

questions.question: Straight-line is the honest choice for:
options: Vehicles that work hardest when new
Assets that serve roughly evenly across their life — equipment, fittings, furniture

subtopics.title: Diminishing Balance, and Additions During the Year

questions.question: Diminishing balance applies the percentage to:
options: The CARRYING VALUE — the base shrinks, so each year's charge shrinks

questions.question: Year two on the bakkie (20% diminishing balance) charges:
options: R19 200 — 20% of the carrying value of R96 000

questions.question: Diminishing balance suits vehicles and machines because:
options: It writes them off fastest overall
They give their best, hardest years FIRST — big years carry big charges, tired years small ones

questions.question: The machine bought 1 September for R18 000 (10% straight-line, year end 28 February) is charged:
options: R1 800 — a full year regardless of purchase date
Nothing until its first full year
R900 — R1 800 × 6/12 for the six months it served

subtopics.title: The Asset Register and Exam Technique

questions.question: An asset register page carries:
options: Description and identifying details, purchase date and cost, method and rate, then year-by-year depreciation, accumulated total and carrying value

questions.question: The register relates to the ledger the way:
options: The CRJ relates to the CPJ
The debtors LIST relates to Debtors CONTROL — detail whose totals must agree with the summary
The trial balance relates to the statements

questions.question: An asset on the register that cannot be produced on inspection signals:
options: Possible theft or loss — the register page has a question to answer

questions.question: The wording that identifies the method: "on cost" versus "on carrying value" means:
options: "On cost" is diminishing balance; "on carrying value" is straight-line
"On cost" is straight-line; "on carrying value" (or "diminishing balance") is the shrinking base

subtopics.title: The Bakkie That Quietly Gets Cheaper

questions.question: The phone that still works perfectly but resells for two-thirds of its price shows that:
options: Working wears value down even when nothing breaks — and the books must admit it

questions.question: Keeping the books at "bakkie: R120 000" for five years would be:
options: A polite lie — overstating what the business owns, which prudence forbids
Correct until the bakkie is sold

questions.question: "Receipt, wear, worth" translates to:
options: Cost price, accumulated depreciation, carrying value — and only the receipt never moves

subtopics.title: Two Ways to Slice the Loss

questions.question: "The same slice every year" versus "always a fifth of what's left" describes:
options: Straight-line (constant base: cost) versus diminishing balance (shrinking base: carrying value)
Two names for the same method

questions.question: On diminishing balance, year three's slice on the bakkie is:
options: R15 360 — a fifth of the remaining R76 800

questions.question: The one trap between the methods is:
options: Slicing the wrong number in later years — say the base OUT LOUD before you cut

questions.question: Diminishing balance charges vehicles honestly because:
options: The new bakkie's big working years carry big slices; the tired repair years carry small ones

subtopics.title: Every Asset Gets Its Own Page

questions.question: "Totals upstairs, faces downstairs" means:
options: The ledger holds one summary line per asset class; the register holds each individual asset — and the two must agree
Assets live on the ground floor
Only vehicles appear in the register

questions.question: The September machine's first-year charge of R900 follows the principle that:
options: Assets are charged for the months they actually served — like paying a worker from their start date
Additions wait for their first full year

questions.question: A register page showing a machine nobody can produce has just:
options: Caught a theft — or started a very serious conversation

questions.question: Beyond control, the register serves the owner's decisions by:
options: Setting the selling prices of stock
Holding each asset's age, remaining value and history — the facts behind replace-or-repair
